title: Task contract (key fields)
description: Lightweight JSON Schema for contract-first task contracts. See docs/standard.md for normative rules.

task_id.description: Stable unique id for this task across retries.

supervisor.description: Accountable approver (user, team, or role id).

identity_selection.description: Supervisor record: use an existing allowed identity or create a new one before execution; rationale ties expertise and boundary to the task.

decision.description: Whether an existing identity was selected or a new named identity was created for this task.

chosen_execution_id.description: Primary execution_id bound for this run after selection.

rationale.description: Why this identity's expertise/domain and boundary fit the task, or why creation was required.

expertise_match_notes.description: Optional detail on domain fit, tool familiarity, or risk.

boundary_monitoring.description: Anti-blur checkpoints during execution; restate identity boundary and contract limits.

checkpoints.description: When to re-verify scope, e.g. time triggers, step counts, or before side effects.

supervisor_role.description: Posture of the main supervisor/orchestrator: control plane (non-execution by default) vs mixed modes. See docs/standard.md §1.1.

direct_execution_policy.description: Whether the supervisor may mutate reality directly, or only via a documented execution bridge. See docs/standard.md §1.1.

execution_bridge.description: When direct supervisor path mutates state because no bound executor is available: narrow written exception with verification and teardown. See docs/standard.md §1.1.

active.description: Whether a one-off bridge is in effect for this task.

justification.description: Why no suitable bound executor; unavoidable direct action only.

scope.description: Minimum mutable surface; time bounds if relevant.

mutation_permission.description: Explicitly allowed mutations under the bridge.

rollback_or_containment.description: How to undo, contain blast radius, or limit blast.

verification.description: Steps to verify outcome before bridge is considered complete.

revocation.description: Immediate post-completion revocation of elevated access, one-off creds, or role.

violation_policy.description: Closure policy for detected violations. See docs/standard.md §8.

closure_requires_violation_record_when_d.description: When true, conformant workflows must block or flag task/review acceptance until each detected violation has a filed structured record linked to this task.

record_template.description: Optional URI or path to the violation record template (e.g. templates/violation-record.md).

violation_records.description: Links or embedded refs to filed violation records for this task; required before closure when violations were detected.

violation_id.description: Stable id matching the filed record.

record_uri.description: Path, ticket URL, or object id where the structured record lives.

filed_at.description: ISO 8601 when the record was filed.

status.description: Workflow state of the violation (e.g. filed, contained, remediated).

visual_marker.description: Emoji and/or color or UI token for operator recognition.

expertise_domain.description: What this identity is for on this task (skills, repos, risk class).

communication_style.description: Expected reporting style for this identity.

execution_boundary.description: Precise in-scope vs out-of-scope statement for this identity on this task.

allowed_resources.description: Narrow list of paths, tools, accounts aligned with the contract.

forbidden_resources.description: Explicit denies for this identity; must not exceed contract exclusions.

executor_stop_conditions.description: Identity-level halt triggers aligned with contract stop_conditions.

executor_escalation.description: Identity-level escalation path; payload should include task_id and execution_id.

allowed_paths.description: Path or resource prefix allow list; empty array means no file/path mutation.
